newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish July priv sector credit growth 13.7 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: Irish July priv sector credit growth 13.7 pct y/y.

text.p: The adjusted annual growth rate of Irish private sector credit rose to 13.7 percent at the end of July from 13.3 percent at the end of June, the Central Bank of Ireland said on Thursday.
End-month banking statistics showed that annual growth in residential mortgage lending rose to 16.1 percent in July from 15.2 percent in June.
Other lending categories also recorded large increases and non-mortgage Irish-pound credit grew by 14.4 percent in the year to July, up from 13.9 percent the previous month, the central bank said.
The adjusted annual rate of broad money-supply growth slowed to 12.2 percent from 13.2 percent, the central bank said.
"The bulk of the increase in both money and credit was Irish-pound denominated. Mortgage lending contributed substantially to credit growth," the central bank said in a statement.
It said private sector credit increased by 497 million punts in July, a 1.6 percent monthly increase for the third consecutive month.
"The main factor contributing to the increase in credit in July was residential mortgage lending which rose by 192 million. In addition, other mortgages grew by 44 million," the central bank said.
It said building societies accounted for the greater part of the increase in mortgage lending in July.

Overdrafts fell by 49 million punts during the month, but loans up to and including one year rose by 84 million and term and revolving loans by 108 million. Lending to the Agricultural Intervention Agency increased by 48 million, the central bank said.

Foreign currency credit increased by 129 million punts, entirely accounted for by the increase in IFSC (International Financial Services Centre) lending, with non-IFSC foreign currency lending falling 47 million.
The broad monetary aggregate M3E rose by 725 million punts or 2.3 percent in July, a smaller increase than in July last year.
"This was partly due to the fact that there were net government receipts this July, in contrast to July 1995, reflecting differences in the timing of corporation tax payments," the central bank said.
It said the greater part of the increase in M3E was Irish-pound denominated, with current accounts rising by 154 million and deposit accounts rising by 382 million.
